newsitem.title: USA: OfficeMax disappointed that store deal off.
newsitem.headline: OfficeMax disappointed that store deal off.

text.p: OfficeMax Inc Chairman Michael Feuer said he was disappointed that his company will not buy the 63 stores that would have been divested if the proposed merger of Staples Inc and Office Depot Inc had been approved.
But OfficeMax, which had ramped up its expansion after Staples and Office Depot announced their merger plan, has emerged as the largest U.S. office supply chain, he added.
"Today, OfficeMax is bigger than either Staples or Depot," he said.
OfficeMax currently has 582 stores and, under its accelerated expansion plans, expects to have 700 to 725 units by year-end.
Office Depot has 572 stores in North America and Staples operates 577 superstores, the companies said recently.
The 63 stores that OfficeMax would have purchased for $108.75 million would have allowed it to enter some new markets, including Baltimore and Washington, D.C.
Feuer said OfficeMax does not plan to target Baltimore/Washington or 11 single-store markets that were included in the deal.
But OfficeMax will continue to expand in Los Angeles, which was included in the sites of the 63 stores.

As it now stands, Feuer said, OfficeMax's deal to acquire the 63 superstores is moot, since it was contingent upon the Staples-Office Depot merger being approved by the U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC). The only possibility, he added, would be if the two companies challenge the FTC ruling in court.

Earlier, Staples said the store sale deal with OfficeMax was contingent upon the FTC merger approval. A Staples spokesman said officials from his company had not yet read the FTC decision and needed ot evaluate all options available.
The FTC said it rejected the proposed merger of Staples and Office Depot, even though the two firms had agreed to divest 63 superstores to OfficeMax.
The FTC raised concerns that the merger could result in consumers paying higher prices for office supplies.
Feuer said he had supported the Staples-Office Depot merger, saying it would have created a more efficient marketplace.

The FTC's rejection of that deal "closes to the door" for OfficeMax to acquire any retail outlets, he said. "Our focus will be in the non-retail area...in ancillary channels of distribution," he added.
